Listen to this article Share The Delta State Government says it has reduced its legacy debts from N463 billion to N63 billion, with plans to clear the outstanding balance by the first quarter of 2027. Sonny Ekedayen, Commissioner for Economic Planning, stated this at the State’s 2026 budget stakeholders’ engagement held on Friday in Asaba. Ekedayen said the achievement of the Governor Sheriff Oborevwori’s Government reflected the Administration’s commitment to prudent financial management and responsible utilisation of public resources. He said that the Government would prioritise roads and critical infrastructure in the 2027 budget to stimulate economic growth and improve access to communities across the State. According to him, the current expenditure structure allocates approximately 70% to capital projects and 30% to recurrent expenditure. He added that the proposed 2027 budget would sustain the emphasis on capital expenditure while maintaining a smaller allocation for recurrent spending. Epiphany Azinge, the Asagba of Asaba, stressed the importance of citizens’ participation in budget preparation and commended the government for its reported budget performance. In their contributions, civil society organisations (CSOs) welcomed plans by the Delta State House of Assembly to introduce legislation regulating housing issues. They urged residents to protect public facilities and maintain environmental cleanliness to complement government infrastructure investments just as they lauded the government for introducing the 13th-month salary, describing it as a significant milestone.
